question: 🇺🇸 Will the Fed raise interest rates in September 2026?
resolution_criteria:
Resolve YES if the Federal Open Market Committee increases the target range for the federal funds rate at its September 15–16, 2026 meeting relative to the target range in effect immediately before the meeting.

Resolve NO if the FOMC leaves the target range unchanged or lowers it.

Resolution will be based on the first official Federal Reserve monetary policy statement issued for the September 15–16, 2026 FOMC meeting.

The size of the increase does not matter. Any increase in the target range counts as YES.

Changes to forward guidance, the balance sheet, quantitative tightening, Treasury operations, or any other policy measure do not count unless the target range for the federal funds rate is also increased.

If the September FOMC decision is delayed beyond the market’s scheduled closing time, the market will remain closed to trading but unresolved until the Federal Reserve publishes the official decision, at which point it will resolve based on that decision
research:
I have enough material and am writing up the report now. It only uses sources dated on or before 2026-09-07. Search results also returned pages dated after that cutoff, and I left them out entirely.

## 1. Resolution source
- The deciding document is the official FOMC statement for the September 15-16, 2026 meeting, posted on federalreserve.gov. It had not been issued as of 2026-09-07.
- 2026-07-29: The latest statement held the target range at **3.50%-3.75%** on a 9-3 vote. Hammack, Kashkari and Logan dissented, all wanting a 25 bp hike. Interest on reserve balances stayed at 3.65%. [Fed](https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevents/pressreleases/monetary20260729a.htm) | [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/07/29/fed-rate-decision-july-2026.html) | [NAM](https://nam.org/fed-holds-rates-steady-in-july-as-three-officials-favor-quarter-point-increase/)
- The range has not changed since the start of 2026. For YES, the September statement must show a range above 3.50%-3.75%. [fomcdiff](https://fomcdiff.com/statement/20260729)

## 2. Current status
- Nothing has settled the question yet. Futures pricing makes a hike somewhat more likely than not, but far from certain. The August CPI (due 2026-09-11) is widely seen as the deciding data point.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-09-05: Trump publicly pressed the Fed to cut rates ahead of the September decision. Markets were still pricing about a 60% chance of a hike. [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/09/05/trump-warsh-fed-september-rate-hike.html)
- 2026-09-04: The August jobs report showed about +162k payrolls against a consensus of about 55k, with unemployment at 4.1%. CME FedWatch odds of a September hike rose to about 58-60%, from 49.4% the day before. One outlet reported about 65% just after the release. One source gives a payrolls figure near 100k, so outlets disagree on the number. [Fox Business](https://www.foxbusiness.com/economy/us-jobs-report-august-2026) | [Roic.ai](https://www.roic.ai/news/rate-futures-traders-add-to-bets-on-september-fed-hike-after-bigger-than-expected-august-jobs-gain-09-04-2026) | [Seeking Alpha](https://seekingalpha.com/article/4943223-august-jobs-report-just-raised-the-odds-of-a-hike)
- 2026-09-03/04: The Dow fell more than 260 points on renewed hike fears, and the 2-year Treasury yield reached its highest level since January 2025. [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/09/03/stock-market-today-live-updates.html)
- Early September: Kiplinger and Morgan Stanley described the August CPI as the bigger driver of the decision. July PCE inflation was cited at 3.7%. [Kiplinger](https://www.kiplinger.com/investing/economy/jobs-report-august-2026-what-to-expect)
- 2026-08-28: In his first Jackson Hole speech, Chair Warsh said elevated inflation could require hikes. He said summer CPI and PCE readings were better than expected but did not show the underlying trend had improved. He gave no timing commitment and no reaction function. FedWatch odds of a September hike moved from about 30% to about 55-56%. Goldman's Hatzius still expected a hold, provided August core CPI and PCE come in around 0.2%. [InvestmentNews](https://www.investmentnews.com/equities/no-fed-relief-at-jackson-hole-warsh-keeps-rate-hike-door-open/267991) | [AP via ClickOnDetroit](https://www.clickondetroit.com/business/2026/08/29/warsh-raises-stakes-for-feds-next-meeting-and-other-takeaways-from-jackson-hole-conference/) | [Morningstar](https://www.morningstar.com.au/markets/warsh-sounds-hawkish-will-there-be-september-us-rate-hike)
- 2026-08-28: Cleveland Fed President Hammack said it is "time for the Fed to act with rate hikes." [FXStreet](https://www.fxstreet.com/news/feds-hammack-time-for-fed-to-act-with-rate-hikes-202608281316)
- 2026-08-07: A big miss on July jobs caused September hike odds to "tumble." [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/08/07/odds-the-fed-hikes-in-september-tumble-following-big-july-jobs-miss.html)

## 4. Base rates
- The Fed last raised rates in July 2023. It then cut in late 2024 and 2025, and has held at 3.50%-3.75% since early 2026.
- Since the 1990s the Fed has rarely surprised markets. It usually moves only when futures price the move at well over 70-80% shortly before the meeting. A hike priced near 60% about 10 days out leaves real uncertainty in both directions.
- Three hawkish dissents in July is unusual. Historically, a group of dissents like that has often come before a policy shift within one or two meetings.
- One headline described a Warsh September hike as something that "has only happened once in the past 36 years." I could not confirm the date or context, and it may refer to a different scenario. [Yahoo](https://finance.yahoo.com/economy/policy/articles/traders-warsh-42-chance-doing-082651946.html)

## 5. Other forecasts
- 2026-09-04/05: CME FedWatch put a 25 bp hike at about 58-60%. [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/09/05/trump-warsh-fed-september-rate-hike.html) | [Fox Business](https://www.foxbusiness.com/economy/us-jobs-report-august-2026)
- Kalshi: one article cites a 57% implied probability of a September hike. Its date is unclear, but it appears to be from late August or early September. [Crypto Briefing](https://cryptobriefing.com/fed-rate-hike-possibility-for-september-meeting/)
- Kalshi CPI market: about 62% probability that August headline CPI comes in above 3.3% year over year, against a consensus of about 3.3%. The article is undated but was published before the release. [Crypto Briefing](https://cryptobriefing.com/august-cpi-probability-kalshi-fed-september/)
- Goldman Sachs: expects a hold if August core inflation is about 0.2% month over month. [Morningstar](https://www.morningstar.com.au/markets/warsh-sounds-hawkish-will-there-be-september-us-rate-hike)
- I could not find a dated Polymarket or Manifold price for the September meeting from on or before 2026-09-07.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- The Fed's pre-meeting blackout period has started, so official guidance is limited. Leaks to the press (for example, a WSJ story) are possible.
- 2026-09-10 (approximate): August PPI.
- 2026-09-11: August CPI, the key data point for the decision. [Crypto Briefing](https://cryptobriefing.com/august-cpi-probability-kalshi-fed-september/)
- Mid-September: retail sales and inflation-expectations data.
- 2026-09-16: FOMC statement, a new Summary of Economic Projections (dot plot), and Warsh's press conference.
- Further political pressure from Trump to cut is possible, along with Middle East or energy shocks. The July statement cited energy-driven inflation.

**Sources:** the links are inline above.

forecasts.reasoning:
* Goldman expects a hold if August core CPI and PCE are around 0.2% month over month.
- **Political pressure:** Trump publicly pushed for cuts on September 5, and Warsh is his appointee.
- **Status quo bias:** The July majority was 9-3 for holding.
- **Volatile pricing:** Pricing was about 30% only 10 days earlier, and hike odds "tumbled" after the weak July jobs report on August 7.

**(e) Scenarios**
- **No:** August core CPI prints around 0.2%. Warsh and the centrist majority argue the trend is improving and prefer to signal a hike conditionally in the dot plot. FedWatch drops below 35% before the blackout ends, and the FOMC holds with hawkish dissents.
- **Yes:** August CPI comes in hot, at 0.3-0.4% core with headline above 3.3%, on top of the strong payrolls. Pricing moves above 80%, and Warsh delivers a 25 bp hike to establish credibility despite Trump's criticism.

**(f) From base rate to final probability**
- **Market anchor:** CME FedWatch (about 58-60%) and Kalshi (about 57%) price exactly this event, so I anchor near 58%.
- **Adjustment down:** I shade down about 3 points for the Fed's status quo bias and the open CPI risk. Goldman's hold-if-0.2% scenario is plausible, and Warsh avoided any commitment.
- **Offsetting factor:** Kalshi tilting toward a hot CPI, along with the hawkish dissents, roughly offsets the political-pressure argument. That pressure is already public and largely priced in.
- **Net:** a small move below the market, to about 55%.

Probability: 55%

**(e) Scenarios**

**(f) From base rate to final probability**

- I start from about 47% for the reference class.
- The liquid markets (FedWatch at about 58-60%, Kalshi at about 57%) cover the same event and are the strongest anchor.
- I shade slightly below them for two reasons. The Fed's strong preference for not surprising markets means unguided 60% pricing tends to resolve toward the status quo more often than the price implies. Political pressure adds some institutional caution.
- Partly offsetting this, the Kalshi CPI market leans toward an upside inflation surprise, and the committee already has three committed hawks.
- Net, I move from the market's about 58% to about 54%.
